messages:
alex: Heads-up — the sample-app is failing on Cloudflare Pages Edge after we switched to the dual-package build. Node examples (CJS) work fine, but the edge bundle crashes inside our auth/retry middleware. @sam any thoughts?

sam: Can you paste the error and package.json exports portion?

alex: Error trace: 
```
TypeError: Cannot read property 'on' of undefined
    at AuthMiddleware (dist/edge/index.mjs:42:15)
    at processRequest (dist/edge/index.mjs:88:7)
```
package.json exports (simplified):
```
"exports": {
  "./package.json": "./package.json",
  "./node": {
    "require": "./cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./": {
    "import": "./esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./cjs/index.js",
    "default": "./esm/index.mjs"
  }
}
```

maria: This screams conditional export resolution mismatch for edge/bundler. Many edge runtimes (and bundlers used by Pages/Workers) ignore the "require" branch and pick "default" or "import" — but our esm build is referencing Node-only globals (net/socket APIs) that the CJS shim wraps differently. The auth layer expects a Node-style stream on Node builds but the ESM edge build has a smaller runtime API and the shim isn't applied.

jen: Maybe we need an explicit "edge" condition in exports so bundlers/edge resolvers get the correct entrypoint: e.g.
```
"exports": {
  "./": {
    "node": "./cjs/index.js",
    "edge": "./edge/index.mjs",
    "default": "./esm/index.mjs"
  },
  "./types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts"
}
```
Also add a top-level "types" field and keep a single canonical .d.ts file to avoid IDE weirdness.

sam: Explicit edge branch would help. Concern: maintaining three builds (cjs/esm/edge) increases CI time and risk of drift. Alternatives: ship a single ESM output that runs on both Node (>=18) and edge, and create a tiny CJS shim that re-exports the ESM for Node consumers that still `require()` — so we only have two artifacts. That keeps behavior identical.

maria: I prefer the single ESM source route if we can guarantee parity for auth/retry semantics. That means: 1) avoid Node-only APIs in the common abstraction, 2) provide small runtime adapters per environment (node adapter, fetch-based adapter for edge). The adapters should live in src/adapters and be wired at build-time via conditional exports.

alex: Good plan. I'll prototype switching auth to adapter interface and open a PR against sample-app to add an edge CI job (Pages + Vercel Edge) so we catch regressions early.

dev-rel-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/pull/412 — adds edge tests, conditional export for ./edge, and a types entrypoint. CI will run on merge.

jen: One more note on typings: use "typesVersions" in package.json for TS path remapping if we need separate type sets for CJS vs ESM consumers, but prefer single .d.ts to avoid duplicated maintenance.

sam: 👍 if we can keep CI green and tests for the auth/retry behavior across envs, I'm happy.

alex: Thanks all — I'll push the auth adapter refactor tomorrow and link the sample-app PR. :shipit:
